item.text: The current structure is already fairly clean, so I’m choosing a refactor that changes the shape of the code rather than just renaming internals: the CLI will become a real entrypoint that parses dimensions from arguments instead of hardcoding a sample. I’ll keep the library API stable and add focused tests around the parser behavior.
I’ve added the CLI parser. I’m cleaning the small fallout now and expanding the tests so the new argument handling is actually covered, not just present in the code.

I caught a subtle correctness issue in the new value object: a record wrapping an `int[]` doesn’t get deep equality semantics, so two identical dimension lists would not compare equal. I’m replacing it with a small final class so the type behaves like a true value object.
I’ve swapped the value object to a proper class. I’m updating the test coverage to assert the semantic behavior that matters now: defensive copying and deep equality on dimension lists.
I’m polishing the CLI failure mode too. Right now it would throw on bad input, which is awkward for a user-facing entrypoint, so I’m making it report a clear usage message instead.
The structural changes are in place. I’m compiling and rerunning the tests now to verify the new value semantics and CLI handling didn’t introduce regressions.
